Container.Name: Sonora
Container.Overview: Sonora is a self-hosted web controller for Sonos S1 and S2 systems. Control every Sonos speaker from any browser on any device, Linux included, with nothing to install on the devices themselves. Grouping, volume, EQ, sleep timers, alarms, music services, local libraries, Sonos Favorites and playlists are all there, along with lyrics, a "This browser" room that plays through the page itself, an S2 upgrade advisor, diagnostics, a choice of themes and twenty languages. It talks to your speakers on your own network; signing in to Sonos is optional. Sonora is not affiliated with Sonos, Inc.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: sonos speaker controller s1 s2 music remote
Container.Requires: Host networking (set by this template). Sonora finds the speakers by multicast, and the speakers connect back to it on the event port, so it must be on the same network as the speakers. It uses ports 50205 and 50206 on the server; if either is taken, set others in the template's Web port and Event port settings.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: The port the page is served on. With host networking there is no port mapping, so change the port here. If you change it, edit the WebUI link under Advanced View to match.

Config.Name: Event port
Config.Description: The port the speakers connect to with live updates. 0 picks any free port.

Config.Name: Allowed host names
Config.Description: Extra names Sonora answers to, comma-separated, such as a reverse proxy's (sonora.example.net, or .example.net for every name under it). Addresses, localhost, .local names and the server's own name already work.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: How much goes in the log: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR.
